predecessors.name: Argentine Confederation
predecessors.text: Buenos Aires province, which the Confederation's government lost in the revolt of 11 September 1852 (the Confederation's 1846 outline minus its 1853 outline, as its own dossier writes it)

successors.name: Argentine Confederation
successors.text: the whole State, reunified with the Confederation, which became the Argentine Republic

ledger.x: 11 September 1852: Buenos Aires overthrows the Confederation's government and secedes.
1 December 1852: Colonel Hilario Lagos besieges Buenos Aires.
12 July 1853: Urquiza calls off the siege.
1857: the south-west pampas appear inside the State's outline.
23 October 1859: the Confederation defeats Buenos Aires at Cepeda.
11 November 1859: the Pact of San José de Flores.
1861: Mitre's army fights the Confederation at Pavón.
12 December 1861: Buenos Aires returns to the Confederation, which becomes the Argentine Republic.
12 December 1861: the State of Buenos Aires ends and its land passes to the Argentine Confederation, now the Republic.

wars.name: Siege of Buenos Aires (1852–1853)
wars.outcome: The siege fails: Lagos's besiegers lose the Confederation's blockading flotilla to bribery (20 June 1853) and Urquiza calls off the siege on 12 July 1853; Buenos Aires stays separate.

wars.name: Battle of Cepeda (1859)
wars.outcome: Confederation victory on 23 October 1859 under Urquiza over Mitre; the Pact of San José de Flores of 11 November reincorporated Buenos Aires de jure, with privileges.

wars.name: Battle of Pavón (1861)
wars.outcome: Buenos Aires wins at Pavón in 1861 and rejoins the Confederation; reunification is dated 12 December 1861.
